newsitem.title: USA: GNA Corp CEO to join Vermont life insurer.
newsitem.headline: GNA Corp CEO to join Vermont life insurer.

text.p: National Life of Vermon said it expects to name GNA Corp chairman and chief executive Patrick Welch as its new chairman and chief executive.
Welch's election is expected to take place at the upcoming meeting of the National Life board of directors on Friday, February 7, following the annual meeting of policyowners, the company said.
GNA Corp is a subsidiary of General Electric Co's GE Capital Corp.

Welch, 49, will succeed Frederic Bertrand, who has served as chairman and chief executive of the 147-year-old mutual life insurer for the past 10 years and who announced his plans for retirement last September.
Welch "brings to us a solid strategic understanding of all aspects of the life insurance business," said David Coates, chairman of the executive committee of National Life of Vermont.
"His work at GNA was extremely bold, and verifies his effectiveness in building upon a company's strengths," he said.

"We are confident that he is the right person not only to lead National Life into the next century, but to help make certain the company continues to develop and enhance its long-standing traditions of integrity, quality and excellence," he said.
Under Welch, GNA grew through internal expansion and external acquisitions from 6.5 billion in assets in 1992 to $40 billion in 1996, National Life of Vermont said.

Under GE Capital's ownership, GNA led the acquisition and integration of several insurance companies, including United Pacific Life, three insurance companies owned by Harcourt General, Amex Life, Life of Virginia and First Colony Corp.
